title: Urfa kebabi
subtitle: Grilled minced lamb kebabs with Urfa chilli
excerpt: Urfa kebabi are grilled Turkish minced lamb skewers, spiced with Urfa chilli (aleppo pepper), onion, and parsley. The dark, slightly sweet heat of Urfa chilli is what defines these kebabs and sets them apart from a plain kofte. They need nothing except flatbread and yoghurt.
sourceNotes: Aylin Oney Tan, A Taste of Sun and Fire: Gaziantep Cookery (2014). Urfa kebabi documented as a signature dish of southeastern Turkish kebab culture. Paula Wolfert, The Cooking of the Eastern Mediterranean (1994). Notes on the dried chilli varieties used across the region.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked shaped kebabs on skewers. Cook from frozen, adding three minutes to the grilling time.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch of the mix and freeze half before shaping.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make and shape the kebabs up to 24 hours ahead. Keep covered in the fridge until ready to grill.
recipe.temperatureNote: Cook on the highest heat your grill or griddle can reach.

content.text: Urfa kebabi are minced lamb skewers spiced with the dark, smoky Urfa chilli from southeastern Turkey. The chilli gives a mild heat with a hint of sweetness and chocolate that plain chilli flakes do not have; aleppo pepper is the closest substitute. The lamb is shaped around flat metal skewers, grilled quickly on high heat, and served with flatbread and yoghurt.

items.prepNote: coarsely grated, excess liquid squeezed out
or Urfa chilli flakes if available

content.text: Grate {{onion}} coarsely and squeeze out as much liquid as possible in a clean cloth. Combine with {{lamb-mince}}, {{parsley-flat}}, {{aleppo-pepper}}, {{cumin-ground}}, {{black-pepper}}, and {{sea-salt-fine}}.

Knead the mixture firmly for two to three minutes until it becomes sticky and holds together. This step is important: the kneading develops the myosin in the lamb so the kebab holds its shape on the skewer without egg or breadcrumbs. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Heat a griddle pan or grill to the highest heat. Divide the mix into eight portions. With wet hands, mould each portion around a flat metal skewer in a sausage shape about 15 cm long, pressing firmly.
Grill for four to five minutes per side until well charred outside and just cooked through. Rest for five minutes.
Slide the kebabs off the skewers onto warm {{pitta-bread}}. Serve with {{plain-yoghurt}}, {{tomato}}, and a scatter of {{sumac}} if using.

items.symptom: The kebabs fall off the skewer when turned
items.cause: Mix not kneaded enough or too much onion liquid left in
items.fix: Knead until the mixture is very sticky and holds a shape. Squeeze all the liquid from the onion before mixing.

items.symptom: The kebabs are dry and dense
items.fix: Use lamb mince with at least 20% fat. Pull off the heat when the centre reads 68 to 70 degrees.

items.symptom: The chilli flavour is barely present
items.cause: Aleppo pepper is mild; the quantity needs to be generous
items.fix: Urfa chilli should be noticeable. Increase to 3 teaspoons of aleppo pepper for a more pronounced flavour.

items.symptom: The outside is charred but the centre is still raw
items.cause: Shaped too thick or grill not hot enough initially
items.fix: Mould kebabs no thicker than 2.5 cm across. The grill must be fully preheated before the kebabs go on.

content.text: Urfa kebabi takes its name from Sanliurfa, a city in southeastern Turkey near the Syrian border and one of the main centres of Turkish kebab culture. The city is known for its lamb dishes and its local chilli. Urfa biber (Urfa pepper) is dried in two stages, giving it a dark, slightly oily texture and a heat with hints of tobacco and dried fruit. It is different from aleppo pepper, which comes from Syria, though the two are often used in place of each other outside the region. Urfa kebabi are eaten at restaurants and kebab shops across Turkey.
